Trump has argued Huang had not done anything wrong and insisted his place atop the artificial intelligence company is essential to the U.S. economy.

“All of this suggests Mr. Trump assured the board that his Administration wouldn’t punish the company for possible violations of export controls or securities laws if they rehired the CEO,” the Journal noted.

Huang’s reinstatement led to a major boom in tech stocks on Monday as questions intensified about Trump’s role in getting the executive reinstated and what the administration and the president specifically stood to benefit from the news.

The connection also sparked bipartisan backlash from lawmakers, with many calling for further investigation into the scandal. The tech mogul is also currently facing a company probe .

Huang is slated to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month.

The U.S. economy, the Journal wrote, “should not hinge on one man and one company.”

“That doesn’t eliminate the heavy cost that Mr. Trump’s intervention will exact on the rule of law and national security. Mr. Trump is signaling that export controls are notional, and national security is subordinate to his political wishes,” the board argued.

“We’re beginning to understand why Mr. Trump so admires Xi Jinping,” the outlet continued. “He likes the way China’s Communist Party boss can give orders to private companies and ignore the law when it suits his purposes.”

Vice President Vance was also personally involved in the push to reinstate Huang, a source familiar with the matter told The Hill on Monday.

articles.title: Govt proposes battery storage for larger rooftop solar systems
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Govt has proposed making battery storage mandatory for larger rooftop solar installations, with consumers potentially required to install
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt has proposed making battery storage mandatory for larger rooftop solar installations, with consumers potentially required to install storage capacity equivalent to at least 20% of their daily generation, as it seeks to address grid management challenges arising from growing adoption of distributed renewable energy.Under the revised draft Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules, 2026, circulated by the power ministry for stakeholder comments, state electricity regulatory commissions (SERCs) will be empowered to specify the capacity threshold beyond which rooftop solar consumers will have to install energy storage systems. In the absence of a threshold, the requirement will apply to renewable energy installations exceeding 10 kW.The proposed provision will come into effect from April 1, 2028. Officials said the move is aimed at encouraging consumers to store surplus solar power generated during the day for use during evening peak hours, reducing the pressure on distribution companies (discoms) to manage fluctuations in renewable energy generation and procure expensive power to meet peak demand.The ministry has also proposed changes to the net-metering framework, allowing SERCs to levy charges on rooftop solar consumers beyond a specified capacity threshold, taking into account the imputed cost of energy storage and network losses. No such charges will be levied up to the capacity threshold determined by the respective commission.Officials said rooftop solar consumers use the distribution network to inject surplus power during solar hours and draw electricity during non-solar hours without fully contributing to the recovery of fixed costs. “It results in increased cross-subsidisation by other retail consumers. We have tried to address this issue,” said an official.The draft also proposes allowing consumers to install renewable energy generation systems on other parts of their premises apart from rooftops, with installed capacity permitted to exceed their sanctioned electricity load, subject to limits prescribed by SERCs.Govt has also proposed deferring the implementation of time-of-day tariffs to April 1, 2028, for consumers with maximum demand exceeding 10 kW and April 1, 2029, for other non-agricultural consumers.The draft also seeks to strengthen consumer protection by requiring discoms to automatically review unusually high or low electricity bills, where consumption exceeds five times or falls below one-fifth of the average consumption during the previous six billing cycles. Consumers will not face disconnection if they continue paying based on their average consumption until the discrepancy is resolved, which must be done within 30 days.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body:
President Trump celebrated the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a Truth Social post Monday, sharing a meme riffing off the famous image of then-candidate Trump after his attempted 2024 assassination in Butler, Pa.

The photo, which appears to be AI-generated, shows Huang with blood on his face and a fist in the air holding up a red bra, likely an allusion to Huang’s multiple extramarital affairs. A flag bearing Nvidia’s company logo — where an American flag was in the original — waves to Huang’s right as he is flanked by Secret Service agents on either side, as Trump was in the original photo.

The meme appears to make light of Huang’s affairs, which included one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The board of Nvidia reinstated Huang as CEO on Monday after Trump’s direct urging. Members of both parties have called for congressional investigations into whether Huang’s affair was a threat to national security.

CNN anchor Jake Tapper replied to the meme on the social platform X, pointing out that two rally attendees died from being shot at the attempted assassination on the president, even as Trump survived.

“Not only was Corey Comperatore killed instantly, rally attendee James Copenhaver was gravely wounded and died two months ago due to complications from his injuries,” Tapper wrote. “RIP to both men and blessings to their families, and blessings to David Dutch who survived the shooting.”

Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chair Brendan Carr hit back at Tapper.

“It’s called a meme, Jake. You’re trying to fact check a meme,” Carr wrote on X.

Trump and Republicans have repeatedly slammed Democrats and called for the firings of those who joked about or made light of the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk last September, including Carr, who threatened ABC’s broadcast license after Jimmy Kimmel made controversial comments about Kirk. ABC pulled Kimmel from the air but later restored him, and the network is now suing the FCC , accusing it of violating free speech rights.

And after the shooting in Butler, some Republicans directly blamed Democrats’ rhetoric for the attempt on Trump’s life.

articles.title: Can GTA VI Really Cost America $1 Billion? Experts Say Probably Not
articles.summary: Experts question the $1 billion GTA VI sick-day estimate. See the workplace data and where the money is really flowing.
articles.body:
The long-awaited "Grand Theft Auto VI" launched Thursday, Nov. 19, after more than a decade of development and weeks of headlines warning that American workers would ditch their jobs to play it. The prediction is catchy, but can a video game really dent the U.S. economy ?

Truthfully, the numbers are a lot shakier than the headlines let on. Here's a look at where the billion-dollar figure came from, what the workplace data shows and why the economy will probably shrug this one off.

The International Business Times reported the figure as a projection by José García-Montalvo, an economics professor at Pompeu Fabra University. It assumed 1.5 million absences and average annual output of about $70,000 per U.S. worker.

PolitiFact , however, couldn't find a published survey or study backing those numbers or tying them to hard data. The trail ended at a 2025 Spanish news report that never explained or credited its estimate.

BambooHR's platform data, covering more than 3.4 million U.S.-based employees, found that paid-time-off (PTO) requests for GTA VI's release date ran nearly 13% higher than on comparable dates in 2024 and 2025. About 18% of surveyed salaried workers said they planned to take the day off to play, or about one in five.

That's a real bump, but it's a long way from a billion-dollar collapse.

Why the Economy Will Probably Shrug This Off

Political scientist and international affairs expert Daniel Schatz told MoneyLion that the math doesn't hold up under scrutiny.

"If employees use accrued PTO, many will simply work before or after the release date, or take a day they otherwise would have taken later," he said. "The new macroeconomic effect is likely far smaller than the headline implies."

Schatz acknowledged that businesses needing physical staff, such as healthcare, retail and customer support, could feel localized disruptions. Those hiccups call for "planning, not moral panic." In his view, the day looks "much like a big sports final or holiday weekend."

Rockstar had already pulled in $3.79 billion by the end of the first day of sales on Thursday, Nov. 19, according to Take2 Games . Full first-weekend totals weren't available at the time of writing.

Record sales aren't the only revenue story. Console makers like PlayStation and Xbox typically get a boost, gaming accessories fly off shelves and players stuck at home are more likely to order delivery or hit the drive-thru.

articles.title: Gas prices drop to the lowest level since March ahead of Thanksgiving holiday
articles.summary: Gasoline prices continue to fall, reaching their lowest level since March.
articles.body:
Gasoline prices ( RB=F ) hovered at their lowest level since March ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

The price at the pump fell below $4 per gallon earlier this month and has continued to decline as oil prices hover near three-month lows. The current national average of $3.61 per gallon is $0.68 lower than a month ago, though $0.54 higher than a year ago, according to AAA data .

"The national average could eventually bottom out between $3.35 and $3.55 over the next few weeks," said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy.

Some individual states have also moved to suspend gas taxes, providing another tailwind for consumers. North Carolina, Indiana, and Ohio are among the states that have temporarily suspended their gas taxes, helping push prices below the $3 threshold.

"GasBuddy now tracking 4 states with average gas prices at $2.999/gal or lower — all but one of which have gas tax suspensions. NC, IN, OK, and OH are all below $3 this morning," De Haan wrote in a social media post on Tuesday.

Brent crude ( BZ=F ) futures rose modestly to hover near $87 a barrel on Tuesday, while US West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) futures traded above $80. Oil prices have tumbled more than 22% over the past month as signs of diplomacy and easing political tensions have outweighed ongoing shipping risks through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Anthropic and 'Grand Theft Auto VI' launched on the same day. The video game trade is winning for now.
articles.summary: Was it better to hold exposure to this year's record-breaking IPO or what may be the biggest entertainment launch in history? So far, the video game trade ha...
articles.body:
Was it better to hold exposure to this year's record-breaking IPO or what may be the biggest entertainment launch in history?

The two collided last Thursday when AI giant Anthropic's ( ANT ) initial public offering hit the market just as Rockstar Games officially released "Grand Theft Auto VI."

So far, the video game trade has come out ahead for investors.

Shares of Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive ( TTWO ), are up more than 5% since last Thursday. Anthropic, meanwhile, has fallen more than 1.3% from its $83 IPO price. It is also trading below the $79.99 cost of a standard copy of "GTA VI."

Take-Two ( TTWO ) said last Friday that "GTA VI" churned out $3.79 billion in global sales on its first day, describing the video game release as "the biggest entertainment launch in history."

Anthropic's record IPO, which raised roughly $81 billion before any exercise of the underwriters' additional-share option, has quickly shifted from first-day enthusiasm into a tricky debate over a range of factors that may be resposible for the stock's lackluster performance, including insider stock sales, how the IPO launch process was executed, and whether the company's enormous revenue growth prospects can overcome its massive computing commitments.

The speed of the reversal from the new company's 17% first-day gain is notable. Among the 12 biggest US IPOs since 2008, only Uber ( UBER ) and Facebook, now Meta ( META ), broke their IPO prices sooner , according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

By comparison, it took about a month before shares in this year's other monster IPO, rocket maker SpaceX ( SPCX ), slipped below its IPO price of $135. SpaceX's stock is down more than 7% from that level as of Tuesday.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said earlier this month that the company hoped to "underpromise and overdeliver " in its public launch. During the same interview at JPMorgan Chase's Manhattan headquarters with CEO Jamie Dimon, Amodei laid out the immense promise he believes his firm's AI models could one day have not only for investors but humanity. His vision included the hope AI could one day help make cancer, heart disease and other terminal illnesses "relics of the past."

Many investors still remain bullish on the AI firm's promise too. "I do believe this could be the first $10 trillion company," Madhu Namburi, a managing director at General Catalyst and former veteran tech dealmaker for JPMorgan, told Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa on Monday.

articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas mañana, miércoles 25 de noviembre: cuándo es más barata y más cara
articles.summary: Más barato que el martes
articles.body: En el tercer día de la semana, el precio medio de la electricidad se abarata de forma muy notable, con una bajada de 99,26 euros respecto al día anterior, según datos del Operador del Mercado Ibérico de la Energía (OMIE). Mañana, el precio medio de la electricidad se sitúa en 110,87 €/MWh, lo que representa un descenso del 47,24 % en comparación con el martes, que cerró en 210,13 €/MWh. Este miércoles, los consumidores deben estar atentos a las horas más caras y más baratas para gestionar mejor su consumo eléctrico. Los momentos más caros para consumir electricidad se concentran en la tarde y la noche. Desde las 17:00 los precios se disparan y se mantiene un bloque continuo hasta las 23:00, con valores por encima de los 200 €/MWh entre las 18:00 y las 23:00. El pico del día se registra entre las 20:00 y las 21:00, con 233,58 €/MWh, seguido de las 21:00 (227,52 €/MWh) y las 19:00 (215,93 €/MWh). Por la mañana hay un repunte menor entre las 07:00 y las 09:00, con un máximo de 170,92 €/MWh a las 08:00. La luz es más barata en las horas centrales del día, una excelente oportunidad de ahorro. La franja más económica va de las 11:00 a las 14:00, con 5,83 €/MWh cada hora, y las 14:00-15:00 también se mantienen muy bajas (7,35 €/MWh). También hay precios reducidos en la madrugada, entre las 02:00 y las 06:00, con valores en torno a los 61-63 €/MWh. En total, 13 horas del día quedan por debajo de la media. En el análisis de las franjas horarias del miércoles, destaca una enorme diferencia entre la hora más cara y la más barata, que alcanza los 227,75 €/MWh, lo que subraya la importancia de planificar el consumo eléctrico para maximizar el ahorro. Esta volatilidad sugiere que trasladar el uso de electrodomésticos al mediodía puede suponer un gran beneficio económico para los consumidores.

articles.title: House Democrat: Trump intervention in Huang expulsion sets ‘bad precedent’
articles.summary: Rep. Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.) called on his party to thoroughly investigate President Trump’s role in getting Nvidia’s board to restore Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO to ensure future presidents cannot do the same. “It’s setting a bad precedent, but this president has set a lot of bad precedents,” Subramanyam told NewsNation’s Blake Burman in…
articles.body:
Rep. Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.) called on his party to thoroughly investigate President Trump’s role in getting Nvidia’s board to restore Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO to ensure future presidents cannot do the same.

“It’s setting a bad precedent, but this president has set a lot of bad precedents,” Subramanyam told NewsNation’s Blake Burman in an interview Monday. “I want this next Democratic Congress to uncover all of the things that have happened, all the corruption, all the fraud, and make sure it never happens again so that future Democrats and Republicans cannot have this level of corruption.”

Democrats and Republicans have called for investigations into Huang because of an extramarital affair he engaged in with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The woman previously led Singaporean AI company Megaspeed, which is now accused of helping China gain access to Nvidia chips.

The Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist Monday after calls for the government to tighten export controls and prevent high-powered chips from reaching China.

Huang is already set to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next week, and some House Republicans are calling for answers on his relationship with the suspected spy. Those investigations are more likely to ramp up and focus increasingly on Trump’s role in the situation once Democrats retake the majority next year.

As a member of the Ethics and Oversight and Government Reform committees, Subramanyam could have a direct role in investigating Huang. He said Monday that he is not jumping to any conclusions, but he suggested Trump’s role will be a target.

“At this point, I want to know everything that happened. I want to know the president’s role in this. I want to know how much he and his family made off working with Nvidia,” Subramanyam said. “There’s a lot of questions that the American people deserve to know.”

Trump has enjoyed a close relationship with Huang since returning to office and celebrated his return Monday by sharing a meme riffing off a famous photo of himself after his 2024 assassination attempt in Butler, Pa., with Huang apparently AI-edited in Trump’s place, holding up a red bra.

The president is heavily invested in Nvidia and likely made millions Monday after Huang’s return sent the company’s stock surging. The White House maintains that the president’s investments are managed by third parties and that he has no role.

articles.title: Wall Street's 2027 earnings hopes may be dead on arrival unless the Fed blinks in December
articles.summary: Stocks are replaying 2018, only this time inflation keeps the Fed from riding to the rescue.
articles.body:
Wall Street spent Monday buying back the AI trade. The bill for next year's AI spending still comes due in the bond market.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) jumped nearly 5% Monday, its best day since April 2025, as Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia ( NVDA ) sparked a $3 trillion comeback . Stocks were mixed Tuesday, with chip stocks leading tech lower again.

But Monday's rescue came from the White House, not the Fed. Nvidia is "systemic at this point," Naveen Rao, CEO of Unconventional AI, said on Deirdre Bosa Live. "It was a little bit like the banking crisis."

A president can help put a CEO back in charge. He can't make money cheaper. Only the Fed can, and Polymarket traders see a better-than-90% probability of another rate hike on Dec. 9.

Alfonso Peccatiello, founder of the Macro Compass, sees today as "a much more similar setup to 2018 than it was in 2000 or 2007." The big difference is inflation.

By Peccatiello's math, about half of the roughly 17% earnings growth Wall Street expects next year assumes AI spending jumps 48% to more than $1 trillion.

That money has to be borrowed or raised , like Meta's ( META ) nearly $100 billion stock sale . Companies "need low market volatility and risk appetite to keep issuing to finance their spending," Peccatiello wrote.

He points to telecom, whose spending "fell by 30-40% compared to expectations despite long-term contracts because the financing chain broke down" in 2001 and 2002.

Today's contracts may not hold up, either. Even after Monday's rally, Madhu Namburi of General Catalyst warned on Deirdre Bosa Live that rising rates are squeezing neoclouds, the AI cloud renters Nvidia helps finance. One he wouldn't name "had two massive contracts. One of the contracts just got canceled."

In 2018, the Fed hiked into a nearly 20% drop, then signaled a pause about two weeks later. Stocks were back at a record by April.

This time, the Fed's hands are tied. Core inflation , which strips out food and energy, is running at 3.1% annually versus 2% back then. "The FOMC bar to turn dovish is quite high," Peccatiello wrote.

His script is a bounce, then more pain. "Bears get frustrated, bulls are flocking back in and mocking everyone for not buying the dips," he wrote in the early morning hours of Monday's rally. He expects the S&P 500 to eventually drop toward 6,500.

Credit spreads , the extra yield investors demand to lend to companies, "could have another 100-200 bps (!) to go," Peccatiello wrote. In a BofA Global Research survey, 52% of fund managers expect a hyperscaler to cut spending within six months, and 38% named AI hyperscaler bonds the likeliest source of a credit event.

articles.title: HPE is heading into 2027 with 'tremendous momentum': CEO Antonio Neri
articles.summary: HPE CEO Antonio Neri weighs in on the outlook for all things AI, tech outages, and Nvidia.
articles.body:
HPE ( HPE ) had the unenviable honor of reporting earnings inside one of the most volatile tech news moments perhaps ever this week.

All things considered, the company handled the moment well — and, importantly, drove home the view that AI demand remains very strong.

"We are entering 2027 with tremendous momentum," HPE CEO Antonio Neri said on Sozzi Unleashed .

HPE is making a pretty compelling case that it deserves to be seen as an AI build-out winner, even if the market may see otherwise for one day.

The company just delivered a strong fiscal fourth quarter, with revenue climbing 50% year over year. Orders surged 88%. The top and bottom lines comfortably beat analyst estimates.

Neri and his team are getting considerably more bullish.

HPE raised its fiscal 2027 revenue growth outlook to 27% to 35%, up from a prior range of 13% to 17%. Even more important, the company expects growth to shift from higher average selling prices to higher unit shipments as AI systems roll out and HPE's enormous backlog converts into revenue.

Networking is another piece of this story that deserves attention.

HPE expects growth to accelerate throughout the year, supported by Helios deployments, Oracle ( ORCL ) order timing, and stronger customer purchase commitments. Its Cloud and AI business is expected to grow 30% to 40% in fiscal 2027 while delivering roughly 14% operating margins.

The business could get a further tailwind in 2027 as companies race to rebuild infrastructure to prevent the headline-making outages seen in recent weeks.

"Well, obviously when you go through a lot of upgrades, and particularly now, software businesses and firmware, there is a lot of mismatch of infrastructure, that's legacy infrastructure, with new tools, new software that have to be all pretested, configured correctly, and deployed at the pace that you need to do it in order to not disrupt the business," Neri explained. "In many cases, customers are going to decide, 'Look, it's not worth it to me to patch all of these servers. Let me take it out because, anyway, it was already almost depreciated. Let's go with a brand-new set of tools and better security.'"

The company also authorized another $5 billion in share repurchases and increased its dividend by 19%.

Even so, HPE stock fell 16% on Tuesday as investors worried margins in the Cloud and AI business have peaked. Shares are still up 69% year to date.

Neri pushed back on the view that margins have peaked.

Along with the rest of the tech world, Neri is keeping an eye on developments from key partner Nvidia and reinstated CEO Jensen Huang.

"I rest easy to the fact that our partnership with Nvidia is super-strong. We continue to bring innovation together. Nothing has slowed down," Neri said.

articles.title: Trump signs bill to end penny production for good: What to know
articles.summary: The U.S. Mint stopped penny production a year ago. But the new law makes that change permanent.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) – The penny was already on its way out , but now it’s official.

President Trump signed the Common Cents Act on Friday, ending production of the one-cent coin that costs nearly four cents to make.

The U.S. Mint stopped making pennies about a year ago, and the new law makes that change permanent. The bill passed the House by voice vote and cleared the Senate without objection.

“In a single year, making pennies cost taxpayers $85 million more than the coins were worth. That ends now,” bill sponsor Rep. Lisa McClain (R-Mich.) wrote on social platform X .

Pennies are still legal tender, and the Treasury Department estimated last year that roughly 114 billion were in circulation.

The Mint expects to save about $56 million per year in material costs, though it will still make a limited number of pennies for collectors.

The law also allows the Mint to change what nickels are made of, which could lower production costs. Nickels cost around 13 cents to make and distribute, more than double their worth.

For the past year, stores that ran short on pennies had to decide for themselves how to make change. The new law provides a federal standard for businesses and allows them to round cash transactions to the nearest nickel when they can’t give exact change.

For example, a $10.01 purchase could round down to $10, while $10.08 could round up to $10.10. Businesses can also choose to round in favor of the customer, bringing that $10.08 total down to $10.05.

“As a retailer, I am grateful to have established legal guidance on rounding cash transactions,” Scott Zietlow, CEO and president of Kwik Trip, said in a statement . “Every cash transaction that we processed in recent months was a reminder that we needed more clarity from the federal government. We’ve now got that clarity.”

Credit cards, gift cards and other noncash payments are unaffected.

A third, its 9.75% note due in 2031, sank 3.75 points to hit 76.3 cents, a low since issuance in April. And its 9.25% bond due 2030 slid 3 points to 80.9 cents, its lowest since it was issued in May 2025.

On Monday, CoreWeave's bonds rallied following news that Nvidia Corp.'s board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO. Tuesday's trades wiped out those gains.

articles.title: Quants Unwind Bond Shorts as Stock Swoon Drives Traders to Safety
articles.summary: Trend-chasing quant funds are trimming their long-held short positions in US Treasuries, fueling a bond rally as an equity selloff revives haven demand for g...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Trend-chasing quant funds are trimming their long-held short positions in US Treasuries, fueling a bond rally as an equity selloff revives haven demand for government debt.

Commodity trading advisers — which seek to profit from momentum across asset classes — have reduced their Treasury shorts to about half their September peak, a Bank of America Corp. model shows. The $5 billion iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy exchange-traded fund, which aims to replicate trend-following strategies, cut its short duration exposure — a measure of interest-rate risk — to about negative 6.4 years as of Monday, from negative 7.1 years a week earlier.

CTAs, an investment cohort estimated to manage more than $400 billion, have been consistently betting against Treasuries this year as an oil-price spike, elevated inflation and the artificial-intelligence boom pushed 10-year yields to about 5.36% in October — the highest in more than two decades.

Since then, a swift unwind of the AI trade in stocks has clouded the growth outlook, pushing the 10-year yield down to about 4.9% and prompting trend followers to reduce short wagers. The group is still pessimistic overall with the Federal Reserve expected to raise interest rates again as soon as next month.

While the bearish trend in bonds remains intact, "it's a little bit choppier now than it was earlier this year," said Andrew Beer, founder of Dynamic Beta Investments, which manages the iMGP ETF.

The fund returned more than 17% this year through October, with much of the gain coming from long oil positions. Short Treasuries wagers were profitable until October, when the bond rally cost the position more than 3 percentage points and reduced its contribution to this year's return to about 1 percentage point. The ETF is now up about 14% this year through Monday.

Despite the setback, Beer said CTAs still have a "meaningful" bet on rising interest rates, reflecting concerns about sticky inflation and persistent fiscal deficits.

But it may not take much for the remaining bearish positions to unravel. Bank of America's model shows a roughly 20- to 25-basis-point drop in yields across the curve "would likely unwind most of the remaining shorts," said Chintan Kotecha, a derivatives analyst at the bank.

articles.title: China Southern Airlines unit to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 planes
articles.summary: The agreement marks the US planemaker’s first major order from China in almost a decade.
articles.body:
China Southern Airlines says its subsidiary, Xiamen Airlines, has signed an agreement with Boeing to buy 50 737-8 aircraft at a list price of about $7.4bn, according to a stock exchange filing.

The purchase agreement was filed with the stock exchange on Tuesday.

The actual purchase price would be lower than the list price as Boeing had offered Xiamen Airlines a “significant discount”, China Southern said in the filing. Large discounts are standard practice when airlines place sizeable orders with planemakers.

The order follows a commitment for 200 jets that China made during a summit between United States President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing in May. The filing did not say whether this order is part of that commitment.

Boeing had not won a major order from China in almost a decade. Last year China reportedly prohibited its airlines from taking deliveries of Boeing jets. It also paused purchases of aircraft-related equipment and parts from US companies in the midst of a trade war, after Trump unleashed a barrage of tariffs on Beijing.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in September that “there are about 140 [jetliner orders] that are in a good state”, with another 10 orders being finalised.

Trump said on Monday that he thinks China will buy another 250 Boeing airplanes. He gave no details, and Chinese officials have not confirmed any further purchases.

The planes in the Xiamen agreement are scheduled for delivery in batches between 2031 and 2034, China Southern said in the filing, adding that the deal is subject to approval from the company’s shareholders and relevant Chinese government authorities.

China Southern said the order would help Xiamen Airlines seize opportunities arising from its move to the new Xiamen Xiang’an international airport, support the construction of an aviation hub in Fujian province and optimise its fleet structure.

Xiamen Airlines, historically an all-Boeing operator, ended a nearly four-decade-long all-Boeing fleet in early 2023 when it took delivery of its first Airbus A321neo under an operating lease.

In April, China Southern and Xiamen Airlines also agreed to buy 137 Airbus A320neo family aircraft.

articles.title: Jensen Huang apologizes to employees, says he’s in therapy
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees in an hour-long company-wide meeting Tuesday, according to a source familiar with the matter.
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees in an hour-long company-wide meeting Tuesday, according to a source familiar with the matter. Huang was speaking one day after being reinstated at the top of the company he founded three decades ago. He had resigned on November 12 following multiple reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman who US officials feared was a Chinese intelligence asset; and one with a subordinate. But on Monday in a surprise reversal of its decision last week not to reinstate him, Nvidia announced it was hiring him back as CEO. Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang after an unprecedented West Wing pressure campaign orchestrated by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. Trump took credit for Huang’s return in a lengthy CNBC interview Monday, saying he directly appealed to the board on Huang’s behalf. But during Tuesday’s meeting, Huang dismissed the idea that Trump orchestrated his return, saying that the board made the decision on its own. He also rejected the suggestion that his return is because he’s a “tech bro.” Huang said he resigned because he broke the code of conduct, the source said. But just because he’s back doesn’t mean he is “above the code of conduct.” Huang went on to say breaking the code of conduct doesn’t automatically mean a person is fired, and that it’s up to management to decide what happens in each case, just as the board did with his situation. “I made some terrible mistakes,” he said, according to the source, who added that Huang said he also apologized to his wife and children, and was thankful to have a second chance. Huang’s two children, Madison and Spencer Huang, are executives at Nvidia, along with his son-in-law, Nico Caprez. Huang, who told employees that he was in therapy more than hour each day, said the company-wide meeting was one of his hardest ever, but noted the “hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife.” Huang also spent time defending and explaining the unusually flat management structure at Nvidia, in which he has dozens of direct reports and no clearly defined successor. He said the structure reflects the company’s diverse business and gives everyone an “equal say” with him. During his absence, CFO Colette Kress served as interim CEO while the board said they would look at internal and external candidates for a new CEO. Huang took no questions, the source said. However, he paused at one point to tell the people assembled in the room with him that “I need your feedback, do you understand what I’m saying?”

articles.title: Consumer sentiment surged in November: Conference Board
articles.summary: Consumer confidence spiked upward in November, the Conference Board reported Tuesday. The board’s Consumer Confidence Index rose from 91.9 in October to 103.3 this month, a jump of 11.4 points that exceeded experts’ expectations. Economists told The Wall Street Journal they expected a slight increase to 92.2. Fergus McCormick, a senior economist at the Conference…
articles.body:
Consumer confidence spiked upward in November , the Conference Board reported Tuesday.

The board’s Consumer Confidence Index rose from 91.9 in October to 103.3 this month, a jump of 11.4 points that exceeded experts’ expectations. Economists told The Wall Street Journal they expected a slight increase to 92.2.

Fergus McCormick, a senior economist at the Conference Board, noted the index is back to “levels of confidence last seen in January 2025.”

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

McCormick partially attributed the rise in consumer confidence to “lower uncertainty” following the midterm elections , which saw Democrats capitalize on Americans’ concerns about the cost of living and seize control of Congress .

“The gain in confidence was led by stronger perceptions of present and future labor market conditions,” McCormick added. “Perceptions of current and future business conditions also improved sharply.”

Consumer confidence, as measured by the Conference Board, has increased in the last two months after it dipped to its lowest level in more than a decade in September.

In November, the board’s present situation index increased by 13.7 points to 132.8. The expectations index, which is based on consumers’ short-term outlook of economic conditions, rose by 9.9 points to 83.6.

“There’s optimism in the air heading into the holiday season,” wrote Heather Long, the chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union.

While inflation remains above the Federal Reserve’s 2 percent target , gas prices have eased in recent weeks , in line with seasonal trends. A gallon of regular gas in the U.S. costs roughly $3.61 on average, nearly 70 cents cheaper than a month ago, AAA reported Tuesday.

But fuel prices remain above pre-Iran war levels , as a gallon of regular gas cost about $3.07 on average a year ago, according to AAA.

Long said Tuesday’s consumer confidence report is a “reminder just how important gas prices are to the American consumer’s economic assessment.”

articles.title: Chinese tech giant Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, US jury finds
articles.summary: jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiring to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks as it grew into one of the world’s...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiring to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks as it grew into one of the world's biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.

But jurors acquitted Huawei of the most serious charge: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy, a result that the company's lawyer said was a "profound rejection" of the government's narrative that it was corrupt from top to bottom and had a corporate culture of cheating, stealing and lying.

Prosecutors had used the charge, commonly found in organized crime and drug cases, to accuse Huawei of operating illicitly to poach intellectual property and technological secrets from competitors and partners.

The convictions covered allegations that the company did business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions — including Iran and North Korea — and made false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds.

Huawei faces potentially billions of dollars in penalties

In all, Huawei was convicted on 10 of 12 counts. The case in Brooklyn federal court involved no human defendants, but the company could be made to pay billions of dollars in penalties when it is sentenced next September.

"Few crimes are as serious as Huawei's decades-long pattern of endangering U.S. national security, violating the sanctity of U.S. commerce, and impeding the enforcement of U.S. laws," Brooklyn U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. said in a statement.

"No person or company is above the law," Attorney General Todd Blanche said.

Huawei's lawyers said U.S. investigators had used isolated episodes of wrongdoing by a few of the company's more than 200,000 employees to spin a false narrative about a grand conspiracy that didn't actually exist.

Huawei lawyer Brian Heberlig said the company would appeal the convictions but was heartened by the acquittals on racketeering conspiracy and another charge, conspiracy to obstruct justice. He called those not guilty verdicts "a vindication of the company and its good-faith compliance culture."

"The allegations that the government made in this case overreached and simply weren't consistent with the successful, innovative and hardworking company that we came to know and deeply respect," Heberlig said outside the courthouse.

US restrictions haven't stopped Huawei's worldwide growth

It's unclear what effect the verdict might have on Huawei's global fortunes. The company hasn't been allowed to sell equipment to U.S. carriers for years because of security concerns. It has also been blacklisted by other Western allies, including Canada and Britain.

articles.title: Utah moves to dismiss criminal case against Kalshi
articles.summary: Utah is seeking to dismiss the criminal charges it brought against prediction market platform Kalshi and its executives last month, the state’s attorney general’s office confirmed Tuesday. In late October, Utah charged Kalshi, CEO Tarek Mansour and chief operating officer Luana Lopes Lara on 13 felony counts and one misdemeanor count. But state Attorney General…
articles.body:
Utah is seeking to dismiss the criminal charges it brought against prediction market platform Kalshi and its executives last month, the state’s attorney general’s office confirmed Tuesday .

In late October, Utah charged Kalshi , CEO Tarek Mansour and chief operating officer Luana Lopes Lara on 13 felony counts and one misdemeanor count. But state Attorney General Derek Brown moved to dismiss the criminal case this week following Kalshi’s decision to stop trading in the state.

Brown’s office noted that if the prediction market platform were to begin operation in the state again, it may refile the charges, saying, “Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges.”

“Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling,” Brown said in a press release announcing the intended dismissal. “Every company in this space should take note. If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.”

Utah’s recent criminal complaint against Kalshi was not the first time the state faced off against the prediction market giant in court. In February, the company sued the state to block it from enforcing its antigambling laws against the platform.

However, a federal judge in August ruled in favor of Utah , allowing the state to enforce its antigambling rules and rejecting Kalshi’s argument that a federal commodities law preempts state restrictions on prediction markets.

Last month, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) announced it filed a lawsuit against Utah to stop the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets.

“Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” CFTC Chair Michael S. Selig said in a press release at the time. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets.”

The price of gas is up by an average of $0.56 per gallon from a year ago as people travel for Thanksgiving later this week, according to AAA.

The average price of a regular gallon of gas in the U.S. was at about $3.61 on Tuesday afternoon, according to AAA. In comparison, the price of that same gallon was at about $3.07 last year at the same time, a 56-cent difference .

In the last year, the price of gas and other oil products has risen as a result of the nearly nine-month war in Iran. Amid the war, the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the oil and gas industry, has been closed.

President Trump recently said he was leaning toward restarting strikes against Iran after the new year if no deal comes together between the U.S. and Iran to end the war. The president acknowledged that indirect discussions between Washington and Tehran were still happening, but he referred to Iranian officials as “professional tap dancers.”

Trump alleged the Iranian regime was stalling negotiations, saying to Fox News that “they talk all the time.”

“All they do is talk, but it’s all bulls‑‑‑,” the president continued. “They’re more aggressive now than before the election.”

Goldman Sachs predicted last week that oil prices will dip incrementally next year, with Middle Eastern suppliers getting used to how the war in Iran has shaken up the market.

Democrats’ recent victories in the midterm elections also came amid the unpopularity of the war in Iran and concerns about the cost of living among Americans.

articles.title: Customers stocked up on gaming hardware ahead of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' launch
articles.summary: Key gaming launches surpassed Best Buy's expectations.
articles.body:
Gamers flocked to Best Buy ( BBY ) stores this quarter to upgrade their setups in anticipation of new games like "Grand Theft Auto VI" and "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time."

In the third quarter, the electronics retailer reported that sales in its entertainment division — which includes gaming equipment, as well as items like health rings, AI glasses, trading cards, and collectibles — soared 27.5% year over year.

While the highly anticipated launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI" occurred in the current quarter and therefore wasn't reflected in Best Buy's Q3 results, CEO Jason Bonfig told Yahoo Finance that the company saw interest pick up in gaming as customers bought new accessories and controllers.

"Gaming did beat our expectations in the quarter, and we really saw customers getting ready for 'Zelda' and 'Grand Theft Auto VI,'" Bonfig said.

On its launch day, "GTA VI" brought in $3.79 billion in global sales, making the video game release potentially "the biggest entertainment launch in history," GTA's publisher Take-Two ( TTWO ) said .

Ahead of the launch, gaming hardware supplies couldn't keep up with demand, Bonfig said. "It is no secret whatsoever, and you can see it across the industry, that gaming hardware, especially the more premium gaming hardware, the Pro and X versions for PlayStation, and … Xbox, are not products that have all the inventory that's needed to meet demand."

The strong gaming numbers bode well for the rest of the quarter for Best Buy.

The company boosted its outlook for the full year too. The electronics retailer now expects full-year revenue to be between $43 billion and $43.3 billion, up from the previous range of $42.3 billion and $42.8 billion. The company also expects sales growth in the range of 3.4% to 4%, above the prior guidance of 1.9% to 3.0%.

Bonfig did not share exact guidance for the fourth quarter but was optimistic about the timeliness of so many launches at once and key holiday shopping moments.

"Everything we've seen quarter to date and what we saw for Q3 was factored into our guide," Bonfig said. "We've had the two launches of 'Zelda' [and] 'Grand Theft Auto VI' already in the first three weeks of November, but we haven't gotten a Black Friday yet, and we haven't gotten a Cyber Monday yet, so you know how much is in front of us."

articles.title: China’s Huawei found guilty of trade secrets conspiracy, fraud in US trial
articles.summary: Jurors acquit the company of the most serious charge it faced of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy.
articles.body:
A United States jury has convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud as it grew into one of the world’s biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.

However, jurors on Tuesday acquitted the company of the most serious charge it faced: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy. The charge is typically used in organised crime and drug cases, but prosecutors used it to accuse Huawei of operating in an illicit fashion to steal intellectual property from US companies.

The verdict followed a lengthy trial in which US prosecutors argued that Huawei repeatedly stole technological secrets from competitors and partners in the US and elsewhere.

Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to US sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to US government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds.

US authorities had targeted Huawei for years, saying the company posed national security risks.

The criminal case began in 2018, and the following year the US government placed Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology.

Experts have said the case has not undermined Huawei’s business, as the company diversified and emerged as a key player in China’s push for artificial intelligence.

The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defence calling 15.

Huawei and three affiliates faced 12 charges, including racketeering conspiracy, bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations, and conspiring to steal trade secrets and obstruct justice.

Lawyers for the company said US investigators had used isolated episodes of wrongdoing by a few of Huawei’s more than 200,000 employees to spin a false narrative about a grand conspiracy that did not actually exist.

Huawei lawyer Brian Heberlig said the company would appeal the convictions but saw the racketeering conspiracy acquittal as vindication.

“That was the only count that brought all of the allegations together,” and the jury rejected it, he said outside court, saying that the verdict “repudiated the central government narrative in the case”.

It is unclear what effect the verdict might have on Huawei’s global fortunes. The company hasn’t been allowed to sell equipment to US carriers for years because of security concerns. It has also been blacklisted by other Western allies, including Canada and the United Kingdom.

The case emerged in December 2018 when Meng Wanzhou, Huawei’s chief financial officer and daughter of the company’s founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the US, China and Canada.

Meng had been secretly indicted for allegedly misleading an HSBC banker about Huawei’s business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of US sanctions.

She fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero’s welcome. The charges against her were dropped.

The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled HSBC, Standard Chartered and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran.

Prosecutors added new charges in 2020, including that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades.

During the trial, prosecutors tried to prove Huawei stole source code from Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel’s antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by semiconductor company CNEX.

Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu booth at a trade show to photograph a device.

Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng’s deferred prosecution agreement, in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran. She did not testify at trial, though an HSBC banker she met with in 2013 did testify.

The defence argued that HSBC and the other banks knew about Huawei’s business in Iran and were competing for Huawei’s business.

Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having “cherry-picked” a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy.

He said Huawei succeeded through “hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development”.

Huawei has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries.

articles.title: A Raleigh woman just got evicted after her landlord refused to honor a deal made by its AI assistant 'Olivia'
articles.summary: “I’m baffled,” said Laura Mack. “I need a place to stay.”
articles.body:
North Carolina resident Laura Mack thought she had worked out a deal with her landlord to pay her overdue rent at the end of the month. But just a few days later, she was hit with an eviction notice.

"I'm baffled," Mack told WRAL News . "I need a place to stay."

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 5 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

When Mack called her complex's leasing office, an agent told her the deal she had worked out over email was not made with a real person. Mack, who was not aware at the time, had apparently struck a deal with the company's AI agent, Olivia — and Olivia reportedly made a mistake when it authorized an extension on Mack's rent payment.

'I thought it was someone from the office'

As she explained to WRAL News, Mack got an email from Colony Townhome Apartments on Nov. 8 that asked, "What date works for you to pay the full $3,934.17?" After sending her response, which requested permission to pay her rent on the last day of the month, Mack received another email that said, "Paying on November 30, the last day of the month, works."

Colony Townhome Apartments, however, didn't contact her again until Nov. 16, when Mack got a notice of eviction.

In late 2025, Colony Townhome Apartments reportedly told its residents that Olivia would be around 24/7 to answer questions about maintenance and rent. According to WRAL News, messages from Olivia are typically marked in order to inform the recipient that they were written by an AI agent. Mack's rent extension emails, however, didn't indicate that they were written by Olivia.

Furthermore, the emails Mack received made specific references to her apartment, including a mention of a severe leak in her bathroom that took nearly two weeks for Colony Townhome Apartments to repair. That, along with the missing Olivia identifiers, made Mack believe the emails were coming from a real person at Colony Townhome Apartments who understood the inconvenience of the leak in Mack's bathroom and gave her a break.

"I thought it was someone from the office because all my information was in there and it mentioned my bathroom," Mack told WRAL News . "I had plans to have until the 30th to either get it paid or go, because that's honestly what my email said."

articles.title: Jim Cramer reverses course on Huang, praises CEO’s return
articles.summary: CNBC’s Jim Cramer changed his tune on Jensen Huang being reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO following Huang’s resignation from the company amid reports of his extramarital affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy. “We may not like what he did, but he got off,” Cramer said during CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street” on Monday.…
articles.body:
CNBC’s Jim Cramer changed his tune on Jensen Huang being reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO following Huang’s resignation from the company amid reports of his extramarital affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy .

“We may not like what he did, but he got off,” Cramer said during CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street” on Monday. “I’m glad. No, I’m glad.”

Cramer spoke with President Trump on the phone during the show about Huang’s return to Nvidia. Trump said he “convinced” the Nvidia board to bring Huang back, saying he had been speaking with the board “directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it.”

Cramer accused the Nvidia board of “acting hastily” by firing the CEO.

“If they had gotten in contact with you, gotten in contact with the attorney general, I think they might have realized this,” Cramer said to the president. “Why not put him on leave before just executing him? That’s what I was concerned about. Because he is a national treasure, Mr. President. He’s a national treasure.”

“And we have to protect — you know, I protected Elon [Musk] in my first term,” the president continued, referring to the Tesla CEO. “Very big. Elon was protected. I talk about it, and I’m proud of Elon. I love Elon. I think he’s great. You know, 80 percent super genius, 20 percent, he has other problems. But I tell him that.”

Cramer said separately from the interview with Trump that Huang being a “national treasure” — a phrase Trump used to describe the Nvidia head on Truth Social — was the “real argument” in bringing him back.

“I heard the ‘national treasure’ argument over and over and over again until I actually believed it,” he said.

The “Squawk on the Street” co-anchor later wrote on the social platform X that the company’s investigation into Huang was “hasty” and led to “a hanging.”

The comments mark a total reversal from what Cramer said about Huang’s resignation less than two weeks ago. He called it “sickening … that there are allegedly serious people who thought that ‘the board’ should not have forced Jensen to resign … How naive.”

“You are talking about a situation where the Justice Department, even this Justice Department, could destroy Nvidia if he stays,” he wrote in an X post on Nov. 13.

The company welcomed Huang back on Monday, which led to a major boom in tech stocks as questions intensified about Trump’s role in getting the executive reinstated. Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s board chair, said Huang was the “right person” to lead the company and that reinstating him was in “the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.”

Nvidia also confirmed it would still investigate Huang, who the board says “fully supports” the probe and has “committed” to cooperate.

The Wall Street Journal’s editorial board warned Monday that Trump’s “extraordinary political intervention will have legal and political costs.” Republican lawmakers also cried foul over Trump’s involvement and Huang’s reinstatement, as the latter is slated to testify in front of the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

articles.body:
President Trump, who pushed Nvidia’s board of directors to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO despite his high-profile scandal, has already benefited financially from the tech mogul’s return to the company .

Nvidia’s stock , which closed at $125.53 per share on Friday, surged on Monday to a high of $171.05 per share — before it fell to $165.05 at the closing bell. On Tuesday, the company’s stock fell nearly $10, ending the day at $155.38 per share.

Despite Tuesday’s decline, Trump still saw a financial boost from Huang’s return to Nvidia in the form of nearly $40 per share.

As of the end of September, the president owned between 32,000 and 370,000 shares of Nvidia, Inc. magazine reported Tuesday. Monday’s rise in Nvidia’s share price equated to Trump gaining between $1.3 million and $14.6 million.

In September, the president purchased between $101,000 and $260,000 worth of Nvidia stock, according to a financial disclosure the U.S. Office of Government Ethics released last week.

He also sold between $1,000 and $15,000 worth of the company’s stock on Sept. 24, more than a month before The New York Times reported Huang had a close relationship with a woman who U.S. intelligence officials allegedly suspected was a Chinese spy, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.

Jensen Huang reportedly had extramarital affairs with the Chinese businesswoman and two other Nvidia employees. The reports led to the Nvidia co-founder resigning as CEO on Nov. 12.

But the company brought Jensen Huang back on Monday, with its board of directors saying it received assurances from “senior levels” of the U.S. government his return did not pose national security risks.

Trump spoke of his role in Jensen Huang’s comeback on Monday, saying he discussed the matter “directly” with the board of directors.

“I spoke to them. Let me just put it that way, and I convinced them,” the president said on CNBC .

articles.title: Like ‘family businesses’: Inside the Nvidia board that ousted and rehired Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gushed last year that support from longtime board members Tench Coxe, Mark Stevens and Harvey Jones was crucial to helping him navigate three decades of running the company.
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gushed last year that support from longtime board members Tench Coxe, Mark Stevens and Harvey Jones was crucial to helping him navigate three decades of running the company. “They not one time gave up on the company and us,” Huang told the Acquired podcast of the board members and other early employees. Those same supporters have now helped see Huang through his biggest challenge yet — restoring his role as CEO following an unprecedented corporate scandal. But their close relationships have also raised questions about the board’s independence and whether it was equipped to hold Huang accountable and protect shareholders’ interests. Including Huang, nearly half of Nvidia’s 11-person board has been with the company since its early days. Its three longest-serving members — Coxe, Stevens and Jones — saw the value of their combined holdings in the company jump by nearly $2.5 billion from Friday to Monday, after Huang was brought back. His reinstatement marks a sharp turnaround from a week ago, when Jones said the board had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation, and had no intention of bringing him back. And it comes despite Huang’s relationship with a woman that US officials feared could be a Chinese intelligence asset, as well as multiple reports about an extramarital affair with a subordinate. President Donald Trump has also been open about his role in pushing the board to give Huang his job back. “The appearance of the relationship between the board and Jensen is most akin to family businesses that go public — that’s a domain in which it’s not uncommon for directors to be there for a long time,” said Jo-Ellen Pozner, management professor at Santa Clara University’s Leavey School of Business. “But those kinds of companies are not major players in the global economy.” Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, the Yale professor known as the “CEO Whisperer,” on Monday called the Nvidia board’s decision to reinstate Huang a “complete failure of corporate governance” and urged them to resign. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on this story. The Board Aside from Huang, whose board seat was restored along with his CEO title, four members of Nvidia’s board have been with the company for around three decades. That includes Jones, who was named last week as Nvidia’s first-ever board chair after joining the company at its inception in 1993. At the time, he’d been serving as CEO of software firm Synopsys, where Nvidia’s original founders had been customers before they approached Jones to bring his operational expertise to the board of their new company. Coxe and Stevens, early Nvidia investors, have also served on the board since 1993, although Stevens took a two-year hiatus from 2006 to 2008. Brooke Seawell, who previously worked alongside Jones at Synopsys, joined Nvidia’s board in 1997. Having long tenured board members means having a “longstanding mission and espirit de corps that a lot of people pointed to as a source of strength for the company,” said Eric Talley, professor at Columbia Law School and co-host of the Beyond Unprecedented podcast. But “it does set up situations where a board might be very, very reluctant to exercise real oversight over someone who’s now become their old friend and someone who has given them loyalty over the years.” That may be why, for example, the board had been reluctant to challenge Huang’s opposition to succession planning that left them flat-footed, causing investors to panic when news of his affairs and concerns about national security risk came to light. Even many of the board members who have joined, by Nvidia’s standards, more recently, have, by current, typical corporate governance standards, been there a relatively long time. Research on corporate boards suggests that the “maximum efficacy” of a board member peaks around eight to 10 years and then “trails off dramatically,” Pozner said. “Boards that have longer tenures are referred to as zombie boards,” she said, “because the implication is that people then are asleep at the wheel in terms of their ability to engage in active oversight because they become like insiders.” Reinstating Huang Still, Talley noted that when it came to reinstating Huang, the board was in a difficult position: stick with their original decision to move on without Huang and risk angering some of their biggest customers and the president “who can wield a fairly heavy governmental and regulatory hammer.” Or it could reverse course, which “makes the board look weaker,” and puts them at risk if additional issues arise from the ongoing internal, state and federal investigations. Going forward, the board may be mindful of keeping a tight leash on Huang to ensure it doesn’t look ineffective, Talley said. It appointed its newest member, Suzanne Nora Johnson, the retired vice chair of Goldman Sachs who joined Nvidia in May, to lead the National Security and Export Controls Oversight Committee it created last week amid the scandal. Nvidia’s longtime board members also stood to gain financially from Huang’s return. Jones, Coxe and Stevens together own more than 62 million shares in the company, according to data compiled by FactSet based on the most recent filings to the Securities and Exchange Commission. The combined value of their holdings declined by nearly $5 billion from the end of October, before the Huang debacle began, through Friday, before making up around half of those losses Monday when Haung’s return boosted the stock by more than 30%. It is typical for corporate board members to own stock in the company; it aligns their interests with those of the shareholders they represent. Nvidia’s board may have decided that, like for them, Huang’s return was in the best interest of all shareholders given the dramatic decline in the stock price following his exit. However, experts say significant holdings could lead to short-term decision making. Nvidia’s longtime board members have all seen their personal wealth rise dramatically in recent years as the company’s valuation skyrocketed. “Now you’re an insider to that company, your portfolio starts to take on the look of an employee’s portfolio,” Pozner said. “It’s impossible then to separate yourself from the company in a way that allows you to maintain the kind of distance that board independence is supposed to ensure.”

articles.title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 close lower, giving up some Nvidia-fueled gains
articles.summary: The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 closed lower on Tuesday as ​Nvidia and other AI-related shares gave back some of the previous day’s sharp gains.
articles.body: The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 closed lower on Tuesday as ​Nvidia and other AI-related shares gave back some of the previous day’s sharp gains and investors braced for possible new tariffs. Nvidia’s ‌stock slipped 5.9% as investors weighed the implications of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO on Monday following questions about the political and governance risks surrounding his return. Technology fell 2.8%, leading sector declines in the S&P 500, while an index of semiconductors dropped 7.9%. Nvidia’s decision to bring back Huang drove a sharp rally in its stock and the market ​on Monday, giving the S&P 500 and Nasdaq their biggest daily percentage gains since April 2025. Huang had resigned earlier this month following ​revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Reuters reported, citing three people with knowledge of the ⁠matter, that the Trump administration is poised to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major U.S. ​trading partners, and that new import duties on a wide range of goods are expected. “After the biggest rally in months, you would expect some profit-taking. At ​the end of the day, one headline doesn’t really resolve investor questions about the AI trade,” said Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera Financial Group. “The correction that we had last week is a buying opportunity for long-term investors, but we continue to believe it can be a very bumpy path for some time,” Goldman said. The Dow Jones ​Industrial Average rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70. The S&P 500 lost 36.08 points, or 0.50%, to close at 7,201.09, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 356.02 ​points, or 1.48%, to end the day at 23,733.54. Before Monday’s rebound, AI-linked stocks had struggled for weeks as investors questioned the sector’s debt-fueled spending and the returns it could generate. Anthropic’s shares ended ‌6.5% lower ⁠at $81.90, below their $83 IPO price. The AI startup had a blockbuster market debut last week. Additional tariffs would add uncertainty to the market, while investors were also cautious ahead of Wednesday’s Personal Consumption Expenditures report, Goldman said. The administration’s tariffs have contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States. The PCE price index is one of the key inflation gauges watched by the Federal Reserve. Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 97% odds of a Fed ​hike in December, and a 66% chance ​of an additional increase in ⁠January, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch Tool. Retailers were among the day’s gainers. Shares of Abercrombie & Fitch which raised its profit forecast, jumped 19.7%, while Dollar Tree gained 11.2%, also after raising its profit outlook. Healthcare shares also rose and led ​S&P 500 sector gainers. Earlier, a Conference Board survey showed U.S. consumer confidence rose to its highest level in nearly ​two years in ⁠November amid optimism over the labor market and the economy following this month’s midterm elections. Volume on U.S. exchanges was 18.89 billion shares, compared with the roughly 19.50 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

articles.title: Trump set to hit India, China, 14 others with new tariffs after probe
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Eight months after it launched a probe on alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 countries, including India, China and the European Union,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Eight months after it launched a probe on alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 countries, including India, China and the European Union, the US Trade Representative is all set to unveil its findings in the case and propose tariffs.The Wall Street Journal said the US is preparing to raise tariffs this week, with Bloomberg reporting that it may come in as early as Tuesday. Indian officials are keeping a close watch on the outcome of the probe, which is likely to be followed by a set of hearings, before final tariffs are announced, in around 45 days.After the setback in the US Supreme Court over the use of emergency powers to impose "reciprocal tariffs", the Trump administration had launched two probes under Section 301.Section 301 probe: Government doesn’t expect any negative impactWhile additional tariffs of 10-12.5 per cent were imposed on imports from over 50 countries, including India, for their alleged failure to prohibit the import of goods with forced labour, which harmed American exports, the outcome of the second investigation is awaited.Going by the mood here, the government does not expect any negative impact, although it maintains that there is no structural excess capacity in India and the surplus is in anticipation of higher demand in the world’s fastest-growing major economy. In fact, during deliberations with the US government too, officials have made it clear that the government has not provided subsidy or other support to create capacity, while underlining that any country which has surplus domestic production is engaged in exports.The report by USTR will be followed by hearings before the final tariff is announced. In the first probe, India had managed to get concessions with the final levy of 10 per cent imposed, against 12.5 per cent, proposed initially. The outcome of the investigation will provide clarity on Trump’s new tariff framework, although the final levy will be known in around 45 days. Based on the final tariff, governments will engage in negotiations for “trade deals”. India is confident of negotiating a deal where its exports enjoy “comparative advantage” over rivals from the region.While the first set of tariffs related to forced labour have been challenged in US courts, even the second one is expected to face litigation, especially because USTR findings are similar for almost all countries. In the case of structural excess capacity, among the top 20 trading partners for the US, all except Canada, the UK, Brazil and Australia are facing action, with the large European countries being part of the EU. The list also includes Norway, Indonesia, Cambodia and Bangladesh, which are not among the top 20 partners for goods and services trade.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Tata Sons weighs stake purchase, buybacks to unlock liquidity for SP
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran is likely to weigh three options to give its largest minority shareholder, the Shapoorji Pallonji Group,
articles.body: MUMBAI: Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran is likely to weigh three options to give its largest minority shareholder, the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, much-needed liquidity. These include a Tata Group entity buying part of SP's 18.4 per cent stake; a proportionate buyback open to all shareholders; or Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata's proposal for a selective capital reduction of SP's shares, reports Reeba Zachariah.The first option would leave controlling shareholder Tata Trusts' 66 per cent stake unchanged. Either of the others would raise its holding in Tata Sons for the first time in three decades.The first two options only require board approval. The selective capital reduction needs a special resolution of shareholders, then creditor and NCLT approvals. A shareholder meeting currently faces a quorum hurdle, and the process could take nearly a year.A Tata SPV could buy SP's shares, provided it is not a subsidiary of Tata Sons, because section 19 of the Companies Act bars a subsidiary from holding shares in its parent. The purchase would lift the combined holding of Tata companies from the current 13 per cent. An external investor could also buy the shares with Tata Sons board approval. The SPV could fund the deal through internal accruals, debt or equity, people familiar with the matter said.Tata Sons could run a buyback of Rs 17,900cr with board nod aloneRule 11UA of the Income Tax Act would set the price of SP’s shares. It values unquoted shares on the adjusted value of a company’s underlying assets and liabilities. Tata Sons’ listed holdings, including stakes in TCS, Tata Capital and other group companies, would be taken at market value, with no holding-company discount. SP’s stake in Tata Sons is estimated at Rs 3 lakh crore.In a proportionate buyback, Trusts is expected not to tender its shares, while SP would participate, cutting its 18.4 per cent stake. If other shareholders, including listed Tata companies, also tendered, SP’s share of the buyback proceeds would fall, the people said.Tata Sons could run a buyback of about Rs 17,900 crore with board approval alone, based on the threshold of 10 per cent of net worth in section 68 of the Companies Act. A larger buyback would need a special resolution of shareholders.Tata Sons last considered a buyback before the 2004 TCS IPO, at a proposed Rs 7-8 lakh a share. It never carried it out, though. As part of Tata Sons’ 1995-96 rights issue, Trusts renounced their entitlement while SP took its shares, lifting its stake to 18.4 per cent.Under section 66 of the Companies Act, a selective capital reduction would see Tata Sons cancel SP’s shares through the NCLT process, reducing its outstanding equity. The percentage holdings of remaining shareholders, including Trusts, would rise automatically, even though they would buy no additional shares.The reduction could also raise governance questions over whether Trusts’ nominee directors can take part in approving it under articles 115 and 121 of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association. It would raise the percentage holdings of both Trusts and the trustees who are individual shareholders, the people said.A potential IPO of Tata Sons could give SP further liquidity and change the company’s shareholding structure. An offer for sale by SP would cut its holding. A fresh issue by Tata Sons would dilute existing shareholders, including Trusts.The first option would leave controlling shareholder Tata Trusts' 66% stake unchanged. articles.title: Tata, Hyundai, Audi to raise prices on higher input costs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Car buyers usually brace for price hikes in Jan. This year, some are getting them sooner.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Car buyers usually brace for price hikes in Jan. This year, some are getting them sooner. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Hyundai Motor India will raise prices from Dec 1, following Maruti Suzuki's Nov 22 increase. Audi India will raise ex-showroom prices by up to 2 per cent across its range from Jan 1, 2027.Tata's increase averages 0.5 per cent across its combustion-engine and electric vehicles. Hyundai will charge up to Rs 8,000 more on select models and trims. Maruti raised prices on select models by an estimated 0.3 per cent on a sales-weighted basis.All three automakers flagged rising copper prices as a cost pressure during their earnings calls. On Nov 13, Tata CFO Dhiman Gupta said he expected steel, rubber and copper to keep costs under pressure in the Dec quarter. He said earlier price increases and cost cuts had offset roughly 40 per cent of the rise in commodity costs in the first half of FY27. Tata absorbed the rest.On Oct28, Hyundai investor relations head K S Hariharan said copper and plastics were getting dearer even as precious metals eased. He put the year-on-year commodity hit to Hyundai's Sept-quarter margin at about four percentage points and said local sourcing, engineering changes and price increases partly offset it.Maruti's Rahul Bharti flagged steel and copper on Oct 27. The company said commodities and adverse currency movements weighed on its operating EBITDA margin by 0.3 and 0.4 percentage points, respectively, from the preceding quarter. The margin still rose to 9.4 per cent from 8.6 per cent, helped by higher selling prices and cost cuts.Carmakers often announce hikes in Dec for Jan. Last Dec, Hyundai announced a weighted average increase of about 0.6 per cent and Mercedes-Benz announced a hike of up to 2 per cent, both effective Jan 1, 2026. This year's earlier hikes follow a mixed festive season. Overall vehicle retail hit a record, while passenger vehicle registrations fell 7.2 per cent to 7.49 lakh, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations.Money habits form by age 7.
